title: Nebius Shares Surge 22 Percent After AI Cloud Revenue Beats Estimates
excerpt: The Nvidia-backed cloud provider reported a sixfold jump in AI cloud revenue to $582 million, securing four deals averaging over $1 billion each.
body:
• Nebius shares surged nearly 22% after the company beat quarterly revenue estimates with $582.3 million in sales
  • AI cloud revenue jumped sixfold, fueled by four deals averaging over $1 billion each
  • CEO Arkady Volozh said the company could sell its entire planned 2027 capacity at current demand levels
  • Nebius raised its contracted power target to 5 gigawatts for 2026 and plans to add over 1 GW annually from 2027

Nebius shares surged nearly 22% on Wednesday after the cloud computing company beat quarterly revenue estimates, fueled by booming demand for AI infrastructure, larger contracts, and higher prices.

The stock traded between $216.11 and $235.96 after opening at $226, compared with its previous close of $193.23. The rally came a day after larger rival CoreWeave raised its annual forecasts, fueling a broader surge across AI infrastructure stocks as both companies signaled that demand for computing capacity continued to outpace supply.

Revenue Jumps Sixfold

Nebius reported a sixfold surge in revenue from its core AI cloud business, which drove overall quarterly sales to $582.3 million — beating analysts' estimates of $572.75 million, according to LSEG data. The Nvidia-powered AI cloud provider secured four deals averaging over $1 billion each during the quarter, nearly quadrupling its total contract value. Contracts from new customers surged more than ninefold.

https://x.com/StockSavvyShay/status/2087506520573677654

"We are turning rising demand into contracted, profitable growth."

— Arkady Volozh, CEO, Nebius

Asked about growing competition from newcomers such as xAI, Volozh told Reuters that demand for AI computing continued to far outstrip supply, adding that Nebius could sell its entire planned capacity for 2027 at current terms.

Massive Capital Deployment

The company spent roughly $5.7 billion during the quarter on GPUs and data-center expansion, well above analysts' estimates of $4.7 billion. The heavy spending reflects the capital intensity of the AI infrastructure race, where providers are building out computing capacity as fast as they can to meet enterprise demand.

Nebius said AI cloud contracts signed during the period, with annual values exceeding $20 million per megawatt, were expected to come online late in the fourth quarter. The company raised its contracted power target for 2026 to 5 gigawatts from more than 4 GW and plans to add over 1 GW of capacity annually starting in 2027 — enough to power roughly 750,000 U.S. homes.

The company expects more than $9 billion in customer prepayments this year and has secured over $40 billion in total customer commitments.

Broader AI Infrastructure Rally

The results reinforced a bullish outlook across the AI infrastructure sector. Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne noted that demand for AI cloud capacity remained strong despite increasing competition, though he cautioned that the key question was whether that demand would prove "diversified and sustainable beyond the AI industry."

Nebius was originally spun out of Yandex, the Russian search engine company, and has since repositioned itself as a pure-play AI infrastructure provider. Nvidia disclosed a 9.3% stake in the company in July, further validating its technology platform and market position.

What's Next

With AI model training and inference workloads growing exponentially, Nebius is betting that the current demand environment will sustain for years. The company's ability to sign billion-dollar contracts and fill capacity well ahead of deployment suggests enterprise customers are locking in computing access for the long term. Whether the broader AI infrastructure buildout proves to be a durable cycle or an overinvestment remains one of the defining questions in technology markets today.
